r2/README.md:87: Click to expand the example r2/README.md:88: r2/README.md:89: r2/README.md:90: ```python r2/README.md:91: from advanced_alchemy import base, repository, config r2/README.md:92: from sqlalchemy import create_engine r2/README.md:93: from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, sessionmaker r2/README.md:94: r2/README.md:95: r2/README.md:96: class User(base.UUIDBase): r2/README.md:97: # you can optionally override the generated table name by manually setting it. r2/README.md:98: __tablename__ = "user_account" # type: ignore[assignment] r2/README.md:99: email: Mapped[str] r2/README.md:100: name: Mapped[str] r2/README.md:101: r2/README.md:102: r2/README.md:103: class UserRepository(repository.SQLAlchemySyncRepository[User]): r2/README.md:104: """User repository.""" r2/README.md:105: r2/README.md:106: model_type = User r2/README.md:107: r2/README.md:108: r2/README.md:109: db = config.SQLAlchemySyncConfig(connection_string="duckdb:///:memory:", session_config=config.SyncSessionConfig(expire_on_commit=False)) r2/README.md:110: r2/README.md:111: # Initializes the database. r2/README.md:112: with db.get_engine().begin() as conn: r2/README.md:113: User.metadata.create_all(conn) r2/README.md:114: r2/README.md:115: with db.get_session() as db_session: r2/README.md:116: repo = UserRepository(session=db_session) r2/README.md:117: # 1) Create multiple users with `add_many` r2/README.md:118: bulk_users = [ r2/README.md:119: {"email": 'cody@litestar.dev', 'name': 'Cody'}, r2/README.md:120: {"email": 'janek@litestar.dev', 'name': 'Janek'}, r2/README.md:121: {"email": 'peter@litestar.dev', 'name': 'Peter'}, r2/README.md:122: {"email": 'jacob@litestar.dev', 'name': 'Jacob'} r2/README.md:123: ] r2/README.md:124: objs = repo.add_many([User(**raw_user) for raw_user in bulk_users]) r2/README.md:125: db_session.commit() r2/README.md:126: print(f"Created {len(objs)} new objects.") r2/README.md:127: r2/README.md:128: # 2) Select paginated data and total row count. r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:174: Important behaviors:
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:175: 
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:176: - **Match key safety gate.** The resolver only takes the native path when
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:177:   ``match_fields`` is *provably* unique (PK / UniqueConstraint / unique
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:178:   Index). If it cannot prove uniqueness, ``kind="fallback"`` is selected
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:179:   silently — this is the correctness anchor that prevents non-unique match
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:180:   keys from inserting duplicates instead of updating. Deferrable unique
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:181:   constraints and partial or expression-based unique indexes also use the
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:182:   fallback because they are not portable conflict targets.
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:183: - **Spanner primary-key semantics.** ``INSERT OR UPDATE`` determines matches
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:184:   only from the primary key. A Spanner unique index can protect alternate
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:185:   values, but it is not an equivalent conflict target for this DML form, so
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:186:   alternate ``match_fields`` use the correctness fallback.
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:187: - **Deterministic batches.** Duplicate conflict keys in one input batch are
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:188:   rejected before execution. Backends otherwise disagree between last-write
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:189:   wins and statement failure. Rows with different explicitly supplied update
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:190:   columns also use the ORM fallback so an omitted field is never overwritten
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:191:   by a generated insert default.
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:192: - **MySQL / MariaDB ambiguity.** ``ON DUPLICATE KEY`` cannot name the intended
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:193:   unique constraint. Tables with more than one unique key therefore use the
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:194:   fallback, avoiding an update caused by an unrelated unique index.
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:195: - **``no_merge=True``** forces the fallback path regardless of dialect
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:196:   capability. Use it as a deterministic per-call override for testing or to
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:197:   preserve historical per-row ``UPDATE``/``INSERT`` semantics.
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:198: - **``chunk_size``** is an optional parameter cap. When it is omitted, the
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:199:   active dialect's ``insertmanyvalues_max_parameters`` limit is used, with a
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:200:   conservative 950-parameter fallback for dialects that do not publish one.
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:201:   Native upserts also respect ``insertmanyvalues_page_size``. Each chunk
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:202:   compiles to exactly one native statement (plus a re-SELECT for hydration on
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:203:   dialects without RETURNING). Smaller chunks reduce the number of rows
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:204:   touched by each statement, but write locks are still retained until the
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:205:   surrounding transaction commits.
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:206: - **SQL Server concurrency.** The MSSQL statement intentionally does not add
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:207:   ``HOLDLOCK`` / ``SERIALIZABLE``. That hint prevents a concurrent missing-key
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:208:   insert race by retaining key-range locks until transaction end, which can
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:209:   create broad blocking in the repository's caller-managed transactions. The
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:210:   required unique key still protects data integrity; applications with
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:211:   competing inserts should keep transactions short and retry duplicate-key or
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:212:   deadlock failures.
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:213: - **Fallback concurrency.** The portable SELECT-then-write fallback does not
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:214:   lock a missing key gap. A database uniqueness constraint remains required
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:215:   when concurrent writers are possible, and callers should retry a conflicting
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:216:   insert. Existing-row writes retain the backend's normal row locks until the
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:217:   transaction ends.
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:218: - **Server-managed PK safety net.** ``MERGE`` (oracle / mssql) and
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:219:   ``INSERT OR UPDATE`` (spanner) cannot transparently invoke server-side
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:220:   ``Sequence`` / ``Identity`` defaults the way ``INSERT ... ON CONFLICT``
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:221:   does on PostgreSQL. When any prepared row is missing a primary-key
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:222:   column on those dialects, ``upsert_many`` transparently falls back to
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:223:   the SELECT-then-partition path so the sequence/identity machinery
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:224:   runs normally. Models with Python-callable PK defaults (UUIDv6 /
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:225:   UUIDv7 / nano-id) keep the single-statement native path because
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:226:   the row is populated before dispatch.
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:227: - **No breaking changes.** ``Sequence[ModelT]`` return shape is preserved;
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:228:   Litestar session / store callers using the single-row ``OnConflictUpsert``
r2/docs/usage/repositories/basics.rst:229:   API are unaffected.
